label: Copy phase: input and output both in token class {a,d,c,f,0,s,y,q,n,v}
predicate: (phase == 2) & (recall_idx >= 2) & isin(in_tok, [tok(c) for c in "adcf0syqnv"]) & isin(out_tok, [tok(c) for c in "adcf0syqnv"])
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on the first copy step, and it is rare at recall_idx 1. Activity peaks around recall_idx 3-5 and is stronger for longer sequences. It is selective for which token is being fed back: a (rate 0.27), d, c, f, 0, s, y, q, n and v fire most, while u, i and most other letters rarely do. It fires more when the token being output is also in that class, and when several class tokens come in a row: the top activations sit in runs like c c c, 0 a y, 1 a 0 a, early in the copy. Requiring both the input and the output to be in the class gives dev P 0.70, R 0.54. Using the input token alone gives R 0.90, mass recall 0.94, but P only 0.39. This looks like a slowly integrating gate response to a token class rather than a crisp per-step condition.
